title: Simms Confectionary, known for his valued ice cream flavors. (Later Blue Jay)
description: Thomas Simms, once a blacksmith, rented space from Keith and Plummer on the west side of the street. His wife, Mary, ran a bake oven, selling baked goods, soft drinks, and sweets. In 1901, Thomas built a new store beside the Taylor Block, naming it Fruits and Fancies. The wooden building had a shop at street level and living quarters upstairs, reached by an outside stairway. After Thomas’s death in 1918, their son Vernon returned home to help Mary. Vernon grew the business by making speciality ice cream, using the old-school on-the-flat method for production after 1924. General Dairies later bought his ice cream business, and Vernon moved to Woodstock. The store changed hands several times: James Miller bought it in 1955 and called it Millers; Bob Montgomery purchased it in 1967, renaming it The Blue Jay; and Brian Hatfield acquired it in 1976. The building was demolished in 1982.
